findings.headline: Smaller premiums elsewhere on the schedule.

exec_narrative: Coopers Cave Federal Credit Union is compared with 32 credit unions of similar size in New York that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index. Of 7 rankable lines, three sit inside the middle half of the market, four above it (NSF / returned-item fee, deposited-item return fee, stop-payment fee and cashier's check fee). We would suggest one step: review the NSF / returned-item fee, which sits above the market range; the peer median of $25 is the reference point.

callouts.title: NSF / returned-item fee — $40
callouts.stat: Peer median $25 · middle half $20–$30 · range $15–$40 · 100th percentile · n=21
callouts.body: Published as “NSF Returned Item.” At $40 it is $15 above the $25 peer median. Returned-item fees remain under regulatory and competitive pressure, and a number of large institutions have eliminated them. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $25 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Deposited-item return fee — $40
callouts.stat: Peer median $25 · middle half $18.75–$30.75 · range $15–$35 · 100th percentile · n=8
callouts.body: Published as “Returned Deposited Item.” At $40 it is $15 above the $25 peer median. This fee falls on the depositor for a check someone else wrote, which makes it a frequent example in fee-fairness criticism. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $25 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Stop-payment fee — $43
callouts.stat: Peer median $25 · middle half $17.50–$30 · range $10–$40 · 100th percentile · n=27
callouts.body: Published as “Stop Payment.” At $43 it is $18 above the $25 peer median. It is infrequent, but it appears in most side-by-side schedule comparisons. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $25 is the reference point.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Coopers Cave Federal Credit Union with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
